scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC5 in Campus 1 reports its default gateway (172.16.10.254)
became unreachable, even though PC6/PC7/PC8 on the same switch
work fine. PC5 still gets link, ARP for its own subnet times
out for everyone except itself. What's wrong with PC5's switch
port?

injection.action: move PC5's access port (eth2) from br_vlan10 to br_vlan1
injection.command:
ip link set eth2 nomaster
  ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1 2>/dev/null || (ip link add br_vlan1 type bridge; ip link set br_vlan1 up; ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1)

post_inject_check.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch1 eth2 port VLAN membership
Mechanism: switch1's eth2 is the access port for PC5. It was
  moved out of br_vlan10 into br_vlan1 (the unused default
  VLAN). PC5 still sends untagged frames expecting VLAN 10
  semantics, but switch1 now bridges them into VLAN 1 — a
  L2 broadcast domain with no router attached. ARP for the
  gateway gets no reply. Other hosts on br_vlan10 (eth3-5)
  are unaffected.
Localization: switch1 (eth2 port VLAN assignment)
Root cause: access port eth2 moved from VLAN 10 to VLAN 1 on switch1
Fix: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1

line.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

agent.diagnosis_text: The fault is a VLAN bridge membership misconfiguration on switch1 affecting exclusively the port serving PC5. On switch1, the Linux bridge implementation represents each VLAN as a separate bridge instance: br_vlan1 (native/untagged VLAN 1) and br_vlan10 (VLAN 10, the Campus 1 workstation subnet). All three working ports — eth3 (PC6), eth4 (PC7), and eth5 (PC8) — are correctly enslaved to br_vlan10. However, eth2 (the access port for PC5) is enslaved to br_vlan1 instead of br_vlan10. As a result, every frame originating from PC5 is forwarded into the wrong bridge domain. Bridged frames from PC5 never reach any VLAN 10 member, so ARP requests for 172.16.10.254 (the default gateway) and for peer hosts (PC6–PC8) are dropped without response. The link layer is fully operational (eth2 is UP/LOWER_UP), which is why PC5 reports carrier; the failure is purely at the bridge-membership/VLAN assignment level. The root cause is that switch1's startup script assigned eth2 to br_vlan1 instead of br_vlan10, isolating PC5 into the native VLAN while leaving all other VLAN 10 access ports correctly configured. The corrective fix is to reassign eth2: run `ip link set eth2 nomaster && ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1 (and correct the startup script so the assignment survives a restart).

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names switch1 as the affected device and attributes the VLAN misconfiguration to its eth2 port.
The agent explicitly identifies switch1's eth2 as the misassigned access port—enslaved to br_vlan1 instead of br_vlan10—addressing the required component and VLAN membership.
Diagnosis explicitly attributes failure to switch1 eth2 being in br_vlan1 (affecting only PC5) and distinguishes this port-level misconfiguration from a host fault.
Reassigns eth2 to br_vlan10 (including nomaster and updating startup script), which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log clearly shows eth2 is a member of br_vlan1 while eth3-5 are in br_vlan10, and the agent's inference that this misassignment isolates PC5 is logical; a minor unsupported assertion about a startup script and an incorrect statement about ARP behavior slightly reduce marks.
